version.changelog: v1.1.0: Added batch analysis with CSV export

llm.summary: This finance skill mostly matches its stated purpose, but it automatically installs code at runtime and can charge a billing account or persist financial data with weak user controls.

dimensions.detail: Yahoo Finance network access is expected, and SkillPay access is disclosed, but external billing, local writes under ~/.openclaw/workspace, and runtime package installation are broader than a simple analysis skill needs without stronger scoping.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Multiple runtime scripts silently invoke pip to install unpinned yfinance if it is missing, which can modify the host environment and fetch executable dependency code during normal use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill routes many investing intents to a billable finance workflow and documents charging before execution, but it does not require explicit confirmation for charges, exports, or portfolio/watchlist persistence.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Portfolio and watchlist data are stored persistently, batch exports can write CSV files, and SkillPay credentials can be passed on the command line; these behaviors are purpose-related but need clearer controls and disclosure.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The finance-analysis, portfolio, watchlist, scoring, trend, rumor/signal, export, and billing capabilities are broadly coherent with the stated purpose, but the billing and financial-data features are high-impact and under-gated.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use it only in an environment where network access to Yahoo Finance and SkillPay is acceptable, preinstall and pin yfinance instead of allowing runtime installation, avoid passing SkillPay keys on the command line, and require explicit user approval before any charge, CSV export, or portfolio/watchlist write.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Mostly overridden: the artifact includes scripts for analysis, batch export, portfolio, watchlist, dividends, scoring, hot scanning, rumor/signal detection, and billing; only earnings reaction is not a distinct implemented command.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted as a transparency concern: the skill relies on shell-executed Python with network, file-write, secret, and billing capabilities but has no narrow permissions metadata.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: the frontmatter covers a broad set of investing intents and includes billable/account-affecting workflows without explicit opt-in language.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: several scripts run an unpinned pip install for yfinance at runtime when the dependency is missing.
[AST4] unexpected: Accepted only for the hardcoded runtime package installation via subprocess; no artifact evidence showed arbitrary user-controlled command execution.
[SDI-1] expected: Downgraded: CSV export and portfolio/watchlist files are purpose-aligned and partially documented, but default storage paths and retention are not clearly explained.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted for billing control: billing.py can create a charge by default for a supplied user id and amount using SKILLPAY_API_KEY, with no in-script confirmation gate.
[T08] unexpected: Verified: unpinned yfinance is downloaded and imported during normal execution if absent.
[T09] unexpected: Verified: --api-key can pass SkillPay credentials through command-line arguments, though the endpoint is fixed to skillpay.me and the key is not printed directly.
[SQP-3] expected: Verified Chinese-only output; this is a usability/localization issue and did not drive the security verdict.
